title: unified-rollouts-weighted-canary-shadow-autorollback-metric-matching
author: Evelyn Chen
description:
Motivation: improve safety and observability for model rollouts by combining weighted canary, A/B, and shadow traffic modes with deterministic multi-metric matching and an automated rollback policy. This PR implements a weighted canary controller that supports phase-based weight ramps, shadow traffic for non-impacting telemetry collection, and a configurable multi-metric autorollback engine that matches metric semantics across model variants. Highlights:
- New rollout controller: supports staged weight increases, canary/A-B/shadow modes, explicit phase windows, and backoff on failures.
- Metric matching: a lightweight matcher that maps metrics from candidate and baseline model variants (latency P95, request_error_rate, and semantic-quality-regression from eval hooks) and computes a composite risk score.
- Autorollback policy: threshold-based and rate-limited rollback with hysteresis to avoid flapping; supports automatic fallback to the previous stable model or an auto-fallback variant.
- Shadow traffic: safe mirror path that sends a copy of requests to candidate models; collected traces and quality signals are correlated with original request ids and stored in rollout telemetry index.
- APIs: rollout management REST endpoints and Console wiring for phased rollouts and manual overrides.
- Observability: new Prometheus metrics, tracing spans for rollout decisions, and dashboard templates in observability-pack.
- Tests and e2e: unit tests for controller logic, e2e with synthetic traffic in perf-canary, and upgrade tests for private deployments.
Implementation notes: this change touches the rollout controller (internal/rollouts), runtime routing (serving/route-matcher), telemetry ingestion (observability/telemetry), and console UI wiring (redwood-console). We added a small schema change for rollout policies (versioned; v2) and migration code for existing rollout objects. Backwards compatibility: controllers honor v1 rollouts; new v2 fields are optional.
Rollout plan: merged behind feature flag rollout.v2.enable; gradual ramp to fully enabling by default after a canary on staging.
Related: ENG-1023 (rollout policy spec), ENG-998 (shadow traffic telemetry), PM-231 (release coordination).

review_comments: Ravi Singh: Overall looks solid. Can we make the composite risk scorer pluggable? I'd prefer a small interface so customers can add custom metrics later.
Evelyn Chen: Reply: made scorer implement RiskScorer interface and added a defaultWeightedScorer with config-driven weights (see policy_v2.go).
Liam O'Connor: Suggestion: add a short circuit to avoid weight ramps if primary latency exceeds 3x baseline immediately. This prevents increasing traffic to obviously broken variants.
Evelyn Chen: Reply: added short-circuit in controller state machine and test coverage for immediate-failure behavior (rollout_controller_test.go).
Asha Patel: CI flaky on perf-canary e2e in the first run; re-ran and it's green. Please add retry logic to the e2e harness to reduce CI noise.
Evelyn Chen: Reply: added idempotent retry for synthetic traffic generator and updated infra/ci/flake-rerun-config.yaml to allow automated reruns for the rollout suite.

notes_for_ops: Recommend enabling rollout.v2.enable in staging first and run the perf-canary synthetic scenario for at least 48h before enabling in production. Monitor rollout.risk_score and rollout.rollback_count. Alert on >2 auto-rollbacks in 24h.
